- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion bias toward prior 7-day average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate in early days (1–7) when sentiment is positive; cap forecast at 1.5–2σ above recent 14-day moving average.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00/0.33 values, model underperforms; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast.  
- When true outcome drops sharply after forecast peak, model often lags; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
